title: Can someone explain to me why the majority prefers the first half of Full Metal Jacket (1987)?

commenti.body:
For me, the two parts of the movie are so different that having been taken along on the journey of the first half and connecting with those characters and then the hard switch into the second half I'm always like 'hey what happened to that story I was involved with?' So the second part never feels like it's as good because I'm a bit disappointed to have been moved on. 

I'm sure others have opinions with a better critical analysis of the film, but this is what I've felt watching it.

It's a strange preference that I don't understand. The second half is a profoundly devastating result of the characters' transformations in the first half. I admire the entire movie and can't think of a convincing reason why the second half would be seen as inferior. 

[This terrific article](https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20220623-full-metal-jacket-and-kubrick-the-ultimate-anti-war-films) about the movie quotes an academic: "Full Metal Jacket is about the abuse of young men, which has been going on in the military since the start of society. These young men are turned into killing machines," and a Vietnam vet: "They take little butter-balls like me and turn them into killing machines. I went from being a good guy to going over to Vietnam, and laughing at seeing women and children being wasted."

The second half of the movie shows the results of the first half. I wouldn't doubt that people dislike the lack of a tidy ending, a resolution: "There's no Hollywood ending. There's no deeper understanding. There's no sense of learning from the experience really. It's just a sense of pessimism." A lot of moviegoers dislike those kinds of endings, sadly.

The final shot is of the men >!marching aimlessly, singing the theme from The Mickey Mouse Club, marching to nowhere, reduced to a hive mind of lost little boys.!< I love it.

I’ll just speak for myself. My thoughts won’t be very focussed. I thought the second half of the movie was great but there’s just something really special about the first half. The first half is such a focussed portrayal of the way the military uses torture techniques to psychologically manipulate and dehumanize and strip away empathy in the effort to create effective soldiers. 

There had been depictions of the cruelty of basic training before, such as in All Quiet on the Western Front. But while the basic training in that movie shows us the way small amounts of power can turn an average person into a tiny dictator (who is ultimately humiliated when he is faced with real combat), the drill sergeant is doing exactly what he is supposed to — not simply making the soldiers tougher but stripping them of their empathy for the weakest and slowest among them so that they will later have no empathy for the people they are ordered to kill.

It’s also psychological horror where we see things primarily through the eyes of bystanders. The ending of that section is also powerful because we have a short moment of satisfaction in seeing a victim take revenge on his torturer but that is followed by the tragedy of his suicide and gut punch of realizing that Joker and the rest not only stood by and let this all happen but that they were also manipulated into participating this torture.

Again, I think the rest of the movie is important too, but I can definitely understand why people find the first half especially effective and powerful.

Agree with all of the comments but for me more than anything it's R Lee Ermey amd Vincent D'Onofrio, two absolutely stellar performances that dominate the whole film and are the thing that stays with most people after the film. The second half is great but the first half and its incredibly intense emotional climax on first viewing takes the wind out of the second half, making it feel more like an extended epilogue. I think its easier to appreciate the rest of the film more on repeat viewings.
